top_signals.title: The Fog of Tech
top_signals.summary: Mara Karlin, a defense policy expert, argues that war planners’ obsession with new technologies like AI and drones has the potential to make them blind to the realities of war fighting. Using examples from Gaza, Ukraine, and Iran, Karlin shows how this technology trap leads to false assumptions about the future of war.

top_signals.title: The China Price
top_signals.summary: In 1971, as the international monetary system was on the brink of collapse, U.S. Treasury Secretary John Connally told a group of worried European finance ministers that the dollar was “our currency, but your problem.” The dollar had become that system’s official reserve currency in 1944, under the Bretton Woods agreement, making signatories subject to the whims of U.S. monetary policy. Even after Bretton Woods collapsed and many currencies floated freely, the dollar continued to dominate. In the last half century, U.S. currency power has only expanded, as more countries have integrated into the global economy and therefore grown to depend on the dollar. China, reliant on export-driven growth, is foremost among them.
